items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I had stolen out of the trick that Slim Freeman had done

ctx.x: But anyway, I played with them and our conductor was named Lee Langster. He was from Chicago. He was an older man. You know how kids are, these were all teenage kids and they were all, naturally by the leader being older, they all isolated themselves off from the leader, you know. Because he was like a schoolmaster, you know.

So we played for two weeks and in this two weeks being the tenor player I got all the solos, and I was breaking up the crowd everywhere we played. I had stolen out of the trick that Slim Freeman had done, laying on his back and turning the horn upside down and all this stuff, and slapped alonguing and all that. And I'd become the star in the band.
Meanwhile, how were you doing with the reading?
